findings.hypothesis: Halofit is the single largest behavioural leak by conversion quality: only 169 of 3,171 Halofit creations were paid for (5.33%), so Halofit workflows produce roughly 3,002 of the 6,319 lost creations and therefore explain a very large share of the gap. This plausibly happens because Halofit plans require additional prescription/operational handoffs or have shorter allowed time-to-pay windows, letting prescriptions or artifact states expire before payment.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab service_type x expiry_reason and service_type x initial_consultation to measure what share of Halofit creations carry expiry/ERX artifact flags; measure median time from 'had a treatment plan created' to payment attempt for Halofit vs Haloskin; run an A/B test extending the expiry window or adding an immediate one-tap payment reminder for Halofit to see if confirmation rate rises.

findings.hypothesis: Customers selecting cash convert much less often than customers on free payer flows: 235 of 3,370 cash creations were paid (6.97%), so cash-payment orders alone account for ~3,135 of the lost creations. This suggests payment friction or lower payment intent for cash flows, or a strong overlap between cash and services with expiry-sensitive prescriptions.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab payer x service_type and payer x expiry_reason to test overlap (are cash orders concentrated in Halofit or in consultation-driven plans?), examine payment-failure and abandoned-checkout logs for cash-flow attempts, and A/B test a short reservation/hold + one-tap in-app payment reminder for cash customers to measure lift.

segments: plans that began with a doctor consultation (entered 2,419)
findings.hypothesis: Plans that began with a consultation convert worse (244 of 2,419, 10.09%) than plans created without a consultation (684 of 4,828, 14.17%), suggesting consultation-driven plans are more likely to fail before payment — plausibly because prescriptions (ERX) or treatment windows expire in the handoff between consultation and payment.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab initial_consultation x expiry_reason and initial_consultation x time-to-confirm to check whether consultations correlate with ERX expiry; instrument the consultation->plan handoff to record whether a valid ERX was attached and run an A/B test that forces immediate prescription attachment or gives an explicit countdown/prompt to pay.

segments: plans showing expiry / ERX artifact failures (artifact_total 2,216) and user-reported expiry (due to treatment expiry 827, erx expired 361)
findings.hypothesis: A large share of created plans lapses because of time-related expiries and ERX/artifact problems: artifact expiries (2,216) plus user reasons like treatment expiry (827) and erx expired (361) point to expiry or missing/expired prescription records as a common mechanism causing creations to never be paid for.
findings.confirm_via: Drill a cross-tab of expiry_reason by service_type, payer and initial_consultation to quantify overlap; instrument timestamps to measure how often payment attempts occur after the ERX/treatment expiry window and run an experiment that extends or auto-renews expiry in a randomized subset to measure effect on confirmation.

findings.hypothesis: Contrary to the initial hunch, free consultations convert at least as well (692 of 4,839, 14.3%) as paid consultations (236 of 2,408, 9.8%), so free consultations are not the primary driver of the created->paid leak; the leak is concentrated more in service_type and payer behaviors.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab consultation_fee x payer and consultation_fee x service_type to check whether paid consultations cluster in low-converting segments (e.g., paid consultation customers concentrated in Halofit or cash); run a targeted follow-up flow for paid-consultation customers (reminder + one-tap pay) to test lift.

growth_ideas.title: 48‑hour ERX auto‑extension for Halofit
evidence: {"user_reasons": {"due to treatment expiry": 827, "erx expired": 361}, "artifact_reasons": {"handle missing expired status record": 2216}}
growth_ideas.rationale: Halofit shows a very low paid conversion (169 of 3,171, 5.33%) and expiry/ERX artifact counts are high, so giving Halofit prescriptions a short automatic extension should recover many confirmations lost to timing issues.
growth_ideas.description: When a Halofit plan is created with an ERX, set an automatic 48-hour extension that keeps the ERX valid for payment attempts; surface a visible countdown and a single-tap pay button in the push/SMS reminder during the extension window. Track confirmation uplift for the extended cohort versus control.

growth_ideas.title: One‑tap payment reminder for cash customers
growth_ideas.rationale: Cash-pay flows convert poorly (235 of 3,370, 6.97%), so reducing the effort to complete payment with a clear reminder and one-tap in-app payment option should raise confirmations.
growth_ideas.description: Send an immediate push+SMS when a cash-plan is created with a one-tap in-app payment link that pre-fills the order and payment destination; if unpaid after 6 hours, send a second reminder showing any ERX expiry time and a direct pay button. Measure uplift on cash confirmations.

growth_ideas.title: Attach ERX at consultation close
growth_ideas.rationale: Consultation-driven plans convert worse (244 of 2,419, 10.09%) and ERX expiry is a common reason for lapse, so ensuring prescriptions are attached before leaving the consultation reduces expiry risk and raises payment completion.
growth_ideas.description: Require or prompt doctors to attach/confirm ERX before ending consultations for plans that create on the consultation path; show an in-session button to 'Reserve plan and pay' that generates the plan with ERX attached and triggers the one-tap reminder if unpaid. Track confirmation lift for consultation-originated plans.

growth_ideas.title: Targeted re‑engagement for created orders
growth_ideas.rationale: A large absolute number of creations never converts (6,319 lost); a systematic, segmented re‑engagement program can recover many of them without changing existing journeys.
growth_ideas.description: Build a segmented recovery flow that sends tailored messages (ERX-expiry alert, one-tap pay, or phone support) within 1, 6 and 24 hours to users who reached 'had a treatment plan created' but not yet 'paid for the plan'; prioritize Halofit, cash payers and consultation-originated plans and measure recovered confirmations by segment.
